quarterly_data.signal: Eaton's 8-K recasts its 2025 10-K segment information for the new Mobility segment (the legacy Vehicle and eMobility segments), formed in a Q1 2026 re-segmentation. 2025 segment results as recast: Electrical Americas net sales $13,276 million, operating profit $3,972 million (margin 29.9%), backlog $13,246 million (+31%; organic orders +16%, book-to-bill 1.2); Electrical Global $6,815 million, operating profit $1,323 million (19.4%), backlog $2,034 million; Aerospace $4,249 million, operating profit $1,013 million (23.9%), backlog $4,316 million; Mobility $3,109 million (2024: $3,451 million), operating profit $405 million (13.0% vs 14.4%), with a 10% organic sales decline due to weakness in the North American region.
quarterly_data.figure: Electrical Americas $13,276 million sales / $3,972 million profit; Electrical Global $6,815 million / $1,323 million; Aerospace $4,249 million / $1,013 million; Mobility $3,109 million / $405 million

quarterly_data.signal: Eaton's recast 10-K business description: in 2025, 22% of the Electrical Americas and Electrical Global segments' sales were made to six large customers of electrical products and electrical systems and services; 20% of Aerospace sales were made to three large original equipment manufacturers of aircraft; and 37% of Mobility sales were made to five large vehicle and component OEMs. Eaton expects to complete the planned tax-free spin-off of its Mobility business into an independent publicly traded company by the end of the first quarter of 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 22% of Electrical sales to six large customers; 20% of Aerospace sales to three OEMs; 37% of Mobility sales to five OEMs
